newsitem.title: UK: Sterling hits 3 marks, European stocks rebound.
newsitem.headline: Sterling hits 3 marks, European stocks rebound.

text.p: Currency dealers, lured by the prospect of higher British interest rates, traded the pound up to three marks for the first time in six years on Friday with the dollar also hitting a six-year high in its wake.
European bourses staged a strong rally, lifted further by a positive start on Wall Street, after a dull showing on Thursday slowed the recent strong performance. Frankfurt hit a new trading high.

Sterling leapt to 3.001 marks for the first time since April 1991 as initial dismay that British interest rates rose by only a quarter percentage point on Thursday gave way to expectations that more increases were on the way.

While the prospect of a three-mark pound proved irresistible to short-term traders, some longer-term investors were wary of piling in after a year-long rally which has boosted sterling 30 percent against the mark.
The pound eased back slightly to 2.9980 marks my mid afternoon and $1.6970, after earlier touching $1.6980, its best showing since January 10.

"Traders are going for big levels like three against the mark and 1.70 against the dollar because the Bank of England has no choice but to raise rates," said Ian Winship, a fund manager at Scottish Amicable Investment Managers in Glasgow.
"But I'd rather not buy gilts or sterling for my overseas accounts right now as I'm too nervous about it swinging around."

Traders are betting that higher British interest rates will be needed to calm inflationary pressures, making sterling assets a more attractive investment. The pound also benefited from market doubts about the strength of a future European single currency.

The sterling rally against the mark helped to push the dollar up by nearly two pfennigs to 1.77 marks, its highest level since August 1991, before easing slightly. "The dollar's climb today is really all down to sterling/mark," said a U.S. bank analyst.
In equities, Frankfurt regained its form after dipping nearly two percent on Thursday to make hefty gains. Dealers said the rally was likely to keep on rolling as conditions remained ideal.

"I can't think of any negative factors, we have the best of all possible scenarios for the share market," one Frankfurt share trader said. "My only slight fear is that people are piling into the stock market without really knowing what they are buying."

Floor trade in Frankfurt closed up 1.2 percent at 4,040.97 points on the DAX index but dealings on the after-hours computerised IBIS index soared to a new intra-day peak of 4072.12, eclipsing the record set two days ago.
The strong dollar was helping Frankfurt's bull run as it improved prospects for the exporting sector. Investors' optimism was also encouraged by low interest rates and inflation-free growth.

London climbed nearly 0.6 percent after a dull performance on Thursday, lifted by Wall Street and a rally in retailing stocks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.34 percent by the European mid-afternoon.
"Wall Street should help us, but the main driving factor at the moment is the squeeze in the retail and food retail sectors," said one senior dealer.
In Paris, stocks made only modest advances in light trade ahead of the long Bastille Day holiday weekend.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 113.80 yen and 1.7680 marks compared with 113.12 and 1.7534 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 30.2 at 4,798.0.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 48.59 points at 4,040.97. The IBIS DAX was up 70.57 at 4,071.50 points.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 12.55 points to 2,941.64.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $319.50 an ounce, compared with Thursday's close of $319.65. Silver was at $4.39, up five cents.
